description:
Dispatcher for note operations: create, render, edit, query notes in notes/.

Usage: notes [SUBCOMMAND] [FILTER]

Args:
  SUBCOMMAND — one of the operations below; omitted means `new`.
  FILTER — optional case-insensitive substring filter applied to the picker list.

Subcommands:
  new — create a new note and open it (INTERACTIVE).
  copy — pick a note, copy its contents to a new timestamp (INTERACTIVE).
  strip — pick a note, copy it and remove the body, for templating (INTERACTIVE).
  edit — pick a note, open in the default editor (INTERACTIVE).
  nano — pick a note, open in nano (INTERACTIVE).
  last — open the most recently-created note. The only non-interactive subcommand.
  delete — pick a note and permanently delete it (INTERACTIVE, destructive).
  cat — pick a note and print it to stdout (INTERACTIVE).
  pdf — pick a note, render to PDF plus markdown with an ACTION/TASK summary (INTERACTIVE).
  minutes — pick a note, render meeting minutes: TOC plus AGREED/RESOLVED/ACTION summary (INTERACTIVE).
  agenda — pick a note, render a meeting agenda (INTERACTIVE).

Examples:
  ["last"]

Notes:
  Every subcommand except `last` opens an interactive picker and reads a selection from stdin. Without a TTY those reads hit EOF and behave unpredictably rather than failing cleanly. Call ONLY `last`; never call new, copy, strip, edit, nano, delete, cat, pdf, minutes or agenda, and never call the tool with no arguments (that runs `new`).
  To find and read notes without a picker, use `search notes` for pointers and read the returned absolute path directly.
  Rendered output goes to EXPORT_DIR, defaulting to the user's Downloads directory.
  Body keywords a note may carry: ACTION: (ingested by `tasks`), TASK: (already ingested; do not write by hand), AGREED:, RESOLVED:, and !: for a callout.

BLOCKED: new, copy, strip, edit, nano, last, delete, cat, pdf, minutes, agenda. These subcommands are refused and calling one returns an error. Do not attempt them.
